summary: W7 Phase 1 business acceptance handoff: prove key seed recall, closure correctness, unrelated-query safety, and recorded precision through the approved business benchmark before allowing overall delivery.
notes: Global human approval evidence: the orchestrating W7 request approved Phase 1 business acceptance, release gates, acceptance mapping DT-00/DT-18/TS-08, handoff production, and the IntentDesign stage commit.

Coverage matrix: grag-quality-gate functionalPoint.DT-18-phase1-business-quality-gate -> ExplicitAcceptanceTestcase-DT-18; grag-seven-wave-delivery functionalPoint.TS-08 -> ExplicitAcceptanceTestcase-TS-08.
DT-18 boundary: key seed recall 100%, closure correctness 100%, unrelated queries zero forced hits, and precision recorded as evidence rather than as a lower-priority substitute for recall.
TS-08 boundary: W7 and whole delivery are blocked until W2-W6 are accepted and the W7 DT-18 business benchmark passes.

DT-00 mapping is preserved as goal/coherent-reading context through grag-goal and the existing coherent-result evidence; grag-capability remains capability context and is not a downstream implementation target for this handoff.

Selected viewpoints: Application Usage Viewpoint for business-observable query/retrieval acceptance context; Implementation and Migration Viewpoint for W7 sequencing, final delivery gate, and quality/capacity acceptance views.
View bindings affected: grag-quality-capacity and grag-seven-wave-gates remain Implementation and Migration Viewpoint instances with updated W7 business benchmark rationale.
No deliveryStatus attribute was invented; existing runner-owned deliveryStatus values were preserved as read-only state.
No implementation artifacts, test code, scripts, configuration, or contracts were modified in this IntentDesign stage.
